$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2,$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/7a6d4db6774da29f9b89996e348fad61b281737db6b44e9a39efa016fa2f15f3.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}],\,T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7x+2y+az \\ bx-3z\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the standard matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2}$ shown above. What is the value of $a+b?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given the vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7x+2y-5z \\ 3x-3z\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $T$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7x+2y+(-5)z \\ 3x-3z\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+b=(-5)+3=-2.$
